The quickest one to set up — no card needed.

1. Open Google AI Studio and sign in with a Google account.
2. Press “Create API key” and pick or create a project.
3. Copy the key and paste it here.

The free tier resets every day rather than every month, so the monthly limit here is only a backstop in case you ever attach billing.

Be aware that Google may use free-tier requests to improve their models. Pages you send are not private to you.

1. Open Google Cloud Console and create or pick a project.
2. In “APIs and services” enable the Cloud Vision API.
3. Go to Credentials, press “Create credentials” and choose API key.
4. Copy the key and paste it here.

Google requires a billing account on the project even to use the free 1,000 requests a month. Keep the monthly limit below 1,000 and you will not be charged.

Worth restricting the key to the Cloud Vision API in its settings, so a leak cannot be spent on anything else.

The most generous free tier here: 5,000 requests a month.

1. Open the Azure portal and create a “Computer Vision” resource.
2. Choose the Free F0 pricing tier while creating it.
3. Open the resource, go to “Keys and Endpoint”.
4. Paste KEY 1 into the key field, and the endpoint URL into the endpoint field.

The endpoint looks like https://your-resource.cognitiveservices.azure.com — both fields are needed.

An Azure account is required, and it asks for a card at sign-up, but the F0 tier itself is not billed.

Noticeably better than the free translators, especially on short lines.

1. Open the DeepL API page and sign up for “DeepL API Free”.
2. Find your key in Account → API keys.
3. Copy it and paste it here.

Free keys end in “:fx” — leave that suffix in place, it is how the app knows which server to use.

MangaLens is a free, unofficial fork of Mihon that adds on-device translation. It asks for nothing and collects nothing — the best way to help is to report what breaks.
MangaLens has no documentation of its own yet, so this opens the docs of Mihon, the app it is built on. Nearly all of it still applies. Translation is only in this fork and is not covered there.
MangaLens is an unofficial fork of Mihon, licensed under Apache 2.0
